text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 3.2% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 9%. The primary driver was crude oil's 7% drop on Monday following news of U.S.-Iran peace talks, which reduced concern about Middle East supply disruptions. Since refiners profit when they can buy cheap crude and sell refined products (gasoline and diesel) at higher prices, a sudden oil price collapse squeezes those margins even though refineries are running at a healthy 92.8% capacity.

The stock's broader weakness over two weeks also reflects uncertainty around the company's leadership change and upcoming earnings guidance announced on October 29. Refiners face a difficult outlook: while oil fell sharply, the peace-talk headlines suggest geopolitical risk premiums built into crude prices could persist or shift, making it hard for investors to price future margins with confidence.
